To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the glass transition temperature and mechanical properties of borate glasses are strongly affected by the cation force constant, FM-O, and the fraction of tetra- versus trigonal borate species, N4, and that cluster formation in glasses can be monitored by vibrational spectroscopy.

the structure and properties of transition and post transition metal ion (Manganese, Copper, Zinc, Lead, Bismuth) borate glasses depend on the following parameters: the metal-oxygen force constant FM-O (determines Tg, mechanical properties), the fraction of tetra- versus tri-coordinated boron (determines mechanical properties), and the formation of borate pseudophases (determines glass stability).

(i) the glass structure of the binary borate glasses can be characterized in detail using vibrational spectroscopy, (ii) the glass structure correlates with the thermal and mechanical glass properties, (iii) the glass properties are also affected by the metal-oxygen bond strength, and (iv) the metal-oxygen force constant is a function of the metal cation field strength.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and physical properties of transition and post transition metal ion containing borate glasses, which are important in many fields of technology.
the structure of transition and post- transition metal ion borate glasses and their impact on the thermal and mechanical stability.
the structure of borate glasses and their mechanical and thermal properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for glasses of similar N4 content, a higher FM-O results in higher Tg and higher hardness.

borate glasses with low N4 values, such as the metaborate glasses and the Cu-borate glasses, show high Tg and high Young’s modulus values, whereas glasses with high N4 values, like the Bi-borate glasses, have low Tg and Young’s modulus values.
the thermal and mechanical glass properties correlate with the average force constant of the metal-oxygen bond and the fraction of borate tetrahedral units.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mechanical properties of borate glasses are mainly determined by the cross-linking of borate units.
the cations impact the borate structure in a very specific way and this impact has an influence on the glass transition temperature and the mechanical properties.
the mechanical properties are strongly affected by the cation cross-linking capacity (FM-O) and the borate speciations, which are in turn affected by the cations field strength.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cation force constant is a key factor in the determination of the thermal properties of borate glasses, whereas the cation cross-linking capacity is a key factor for the mechanical properties.
borate glasses can be used as a model system to study structure-property relationships in oxide glasses in general, and the impact of cations on the structure of the glass network in particular.
the cations impact the borate structure and the formation of clusters, and the latter is responsible for the enhancement of the mechanical and thermal properties of glasses.
